cards.text: Moses is still speaking to all Israel, across the Jordan in the land of Moab (Deut 1:1, 5). Now he gets practical about how to treat your neighbors. You're out walking, and you spot your brother's ox or sheep straying.

cards.question: You spot your brother's ox or sheep straying. What does Moses say to do?

cards.text: Easy when your brother lives right down the road. But what if he lives FAR away, or you have NO idea whose ox is standing in front of you?

cards.question: What if your brother lives far away, or you don't know whose stray animal it is? What does Moses say to do?

answers.text: Take it home until he comes for it
Sell it and save the money for him
Turn it loose back into the field

cards.question: Moses' rule about returning lost things covers only oxen and sheep.

cards.text: His donkey, his cloak, anything your brother lost and you found: you must not ignore it. I spent YEARS lost in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so I am ALL in on this law.

cards.question: Your brother's donkey or ox has fallen on the road. What does Moses say to do?

cards.text: Then Moses talks clothing. A woman must not wear men's clothing, and a man must not wear women's clothing.

cards.question: Moses says men and women must not wear each other's clothing. What reason does he give?

answers.text: It is detestable to the LORD
It is a sign of mourning
It brings shame on the family

cards.text: Next, a walk down the road. You come across a bird's nest, in a tree or on the ground, and the mother is sitting on the chicks or eggs.

cards.question: You find a mother bird sitting on her chicks or eggs. What does Moses allow you to do?

answers.text: Take the young but let the mother go
Take the mother but leave the young
Take the mother along with the young

cards.question: Moses attaches a promise to letting the mother bird go. What is it?

answers.text: That you may prolong your days
That your harvest may be great

cards.text: A long-life promise, over a BIRD'S NEST. Next up, Moses the BUILDING INSPECTOR: if you build a new house, put a railing around your roof.

cards.question: Moses says a new house needs a railing around the roof. Why?

answers.text: So no bloodguilt comes if someone falls
So the neighbors cannot look inside
So the wind will not blow things off

cards.text: Now come some no-mixing rules. Don't plant your vineyard with two types of seed, and don't wear clothes of wool and linen woven together.

cards.question: Moses warns that planting a vineyard with two types of seed defiles the entire harvest.
Moses has a no-mixing rule for plowing too. What must not be yoked together?
One more rule for your wardrobe. What are you to make on the four corners of the cloak you wear?

cards.text: Now Moses turns to marriage, and things get serious. Suppose a man marries, comes to hate his wife, and accuses her of shameful conduct, saying she was not a virgin.

cards.question: A husband has given his wife a bad name. Who brings the proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate?

cards.text: Her parents stand before the elders at the gate. They say, "I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, but he has come to hate her."

cards.question: Her parents spread out the cloth before the elders, and it shows the husband's accusation is false. What do the elders do to him?

answers.text: Send him out of the city

cards.question: The husband is fined a hundred shekels of silver for giving her a bad name. Who receives the silver?
After his false accusation, the husband is still allowed to divorce his wife.

cards.text: She remains his wife, and he must not divorce her as long as he lives. But if the accusation is true and no proof can be found, it goes the other way, and she is to be stoned to death.

cards.question: If the accusation is true, where is the young woman stoned?

answers.text: At the door of her father's house
Outside the walls of the city

cards.text: Moses calls it an outrage in Israel and says, "So you must purge the evil from among you." Then he takes up a man found lying with another man's wife.

cards.question: A man is found lying with another man's wife. Who must die?

answers.text: Both the man and the woman

cards.text: Next, a virgin pledged in marriage to a man. Another man encounters her in the city and sleeps with her.

cards.question: In the city, both of them are stoned at the gate. What reason does the law give for the young woman?

answers.text: She did not cry out in the city
She did not tell her family
She went out in the city alone

cards.text: And the man dies because he violated his neighbor's wife. But now Moses changes the place to the open country, where a man overpowers a betrothed woman and lies with her.

cards.question: In the open country, the man overpowers the betrothed woman. Who must die?
Moses says the open-country case is just like another case. Which one?

answers.text: A man who attacks his neighbor and murders him
A man who steals his neighbor's ox
A man who moves his neighbor's boundary stone

cards.text: Moses says, "Do nothing to the young woman, because she has committed no sin worthy of death." She cried out in that field, but there was no one to save her.
One more case. A man seizes a virgin who isn't pledged in marriage and lies with her, and they are discovered. He must pay her father fifty shekels of silver.

cards.question: The man pays the young woman's father fifty shekels of silver. What else does the law require of him?

answers.text: He must marry her and never divorce her
He must leave the city and never return
He must serve her father for seven years

cards.question: Moses ends with a law about a man's own family. Who is a man not to marry?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Moses isn't done preaching, friend, and neither is this speech.

findings.problem: Of the 11 choice cards, 9 are multiple choice and 2 are true or false, with no fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Of the 11 choice cards, 10 are multiple choice and 1 is true or false, with no fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop, and the stop repeats Stop 1's mostly multiple-choice pattern.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer ('Take the young but let the mother go') comes entirely from Deuteronomy 22:7, but the card cites Deuteronomy 22:6-7.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: This story card is not the opening card, but it has 3 sentences: 'One more case.', 'A man seizes a virgin...', and 'He must pay her father...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question asks generally 'Who is a man not to marry?' Both wrong answers, 'His father's sister' and 'His daughter-in-law', are forbidden elsewhere in the Law (Leviticus 18:12, 18:15). A baker could argue that either one is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Almost all of Deuteronomy 22 is a series of rules for everyday life. The docs list 'rules for everyday life' as a long stretch that gets one summary card and no choice cards. They also say 'speeches, teaching and key laws' are not long stretches. This passage is part of Moses' speech and is typed Sermons. The walkthrough treats every law as askable.
findings.question: When a Sermons passage inside Moses' speech is mostly a list of everyday laws, like Deuteronomy 22:1-12 and 22:9-12, should those laws be summed up as a long stretch, or does being part of a speech make each law askable?

findings.problem: Stop 2 asks quiz questions about cases of adultery, rape (22:25-29) and stoning. The docs say the app is 'Written for adults. Kids can still play.' They don't say how to handle sexual violence in choice cards or how much detail to ask about.
findings.question: For passages about sexual violence and execution, like Deuteronomy 22:13-29, should Prep ask choice cards about those cases, or sum them up on story cards with fewer details tested? Is there any wording guidance, given that kids can still play?

findings.problem: The last story card is only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse, but it cites Deuteronomy 22:30. The rule says story cards cite the verses they tell, and the docs allow this card to be just the line. They don't say what such a card should cite.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-isn't-over line, what should its 'verses' field cite: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or something else?
